welcome.title: Welcome to Specrails
welcome.subtitle: Your local cockpit for shipping software with AI agents
welcome.intro: Specrails turns an idea into shipped code — and lets you see, steer and trust every step. Describe what you want, get precise specs, run them on rails with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini or Kimi, and decide what to merge. Nothing merges without you.
welcome.flowCaption: Describe → Specs → Rails → Review & merge. Every step streams live, and every result waits for your decision.
welcome.missionBody: One conversation drives the whole app: the agent authors specs, launches rails, checks spend and hands you decision cards. You talk, it operates.
welcome.boardBody: The classic dashboard: specs board, rails, jobs, analytics. Flip between the two from the switch in the left sidebar — same projects, same data.
welcome.localNote: 100% local · single user · no accounts. Everything runs on your machine. Your code never leaves the laptop unless you spawn an agent against it.
welcome.tourNote: This quick tour walks through everything the app can do — about two minutes.

mission.title: Talk — the agent operates
mission.subtitle: Mission mode is the default surface
mission.intro: In Mission mode the whole window is one conversation with an agent that drives Specrails through its own MCP tools: “launch the three highest-priority specs”, “how much did I spend this week?”, “write me a spec for dark mode”. Everything it does is live — rails, specs and cards update as it works.
mission.missionsBody: Each conversation is a mission pinned to a project (or Home for everything). Switch missions from the header, send follow-ups mid-turn — they queue and run in order.
mission.levelsBody: A live level — Observe → Edit → Operate → Autonomous, cycled with Shift Tab — caps how far it can go. It never acts above the level you set.
mission.cardsBody: Launches surface as live cards pinned above the composer: rail progress, then Create PR / Integrate locally / Discard, with a plain-language Review. Spec numbers, jobs and loops in replies are clickable.
mission.workspaceBody: The right sidebar opens Blueprint, Jobs, Analytics, an embedded browser, the terminal and the code explorer next to the conversation — no context switch.
mission.mcpBody: The agent works through the embedded Specrails MCP server — on by default, loopback only. The same server lets your own tools (Claude Desktop, Cursor…) drive Specrails; manage it in Settings → MCP.

builder.title: Start a project from an idea
builder.subtitle: The Builder: blueprint, specs and milestones before a line of code exists
builder.intro: Add Project → New turns the agent into the Project Builder. Describe the idea; it interviews you briefly (or decides everything with one click), proposes product, core flow, platform, stack and milestones, and you approve or tweak.
builder.flowCaption: The commit creates the repository, the workspace and the Milestone-1 backlog — optionally a private GitHub repo too.
builder.cardsBody: “Surprise me” and “Approve & generate specs” appear as cards in the thread; each decision you take stays pinned there as a record.
builder.specsBody: Milestone-1 specs are written in full two at a time, then the whole batch is audited — problem, solution, scope, technical considerations, six-plus acceptance criteria — and a deterministic gate blocks anything thin.
builder.milestonesBody: Launch Milestone 1 and it runs as rails of up to three specs, each stacked on the previous one's branch. Wave checkpoints ask before each next rail — or flip auto-continue.
builder.progressBody: The Blueprint panel shows real counts — delivered, in review, done — never “complete” while anything is unmerged. Later milestones are generated against the real repository.

authorSpecs.title: Turn ideas into specs
authorSpecs.subtitle: Six ways to capture exactly what you want built
authorSpecs.intro: A spec is a description of work you want done. Author one however suits the moment — from a one-liner to the agent doing the research for you.
authorSpecs.agentBody: In Mission mode, just describe the change. The agent reads the real codebase first, drafts a super spec as a live card and commits it when you say so.
authorSpecs.exploreBody: Describe what you want in a chat; a live draft rebuilds itself every turn. A preset slider tunes how much project context the AI sees — from your message only, up to the full codebase plus your MCP servers.
authorSpecs.quickBody: Already know what you want? Generate a complete spec in a single turn. Optionally enrich it with a Contract Layer: exact names, data shapes, invariants and a file-touch list so the agents don't reinvent anything.
authorSpecs.websiteBody: Opens an embedded browser. Hover-select an element or drag a rectangle, and the screenshot, DOM and applied CSS become attachments.
authorSpecs.smashBody: Explode a large spec into a family of smaller sub-specs in one click — each child carries a short summary on its card.
authorSpecs.draftsBody: Park an in-progress exploration as a draft ticket and resume it later; reopen any spec back in Explore to keep refining it.

rails.title: Run the pipeline on rails
rails.subtitle: Isolated lanes, then a review you can actually read
rails.intro: Rails are execution lanes — up to twelve, created on demand. Drop specs on a rail and press ▶ Play, or Launch all idle rails in parallel. Each run works in its own git worktree, never in your checkout.
rails.flowCaption: Every phase streams live. At the end the work stays on its branch and the app asks you what to do — Specrails produces PRs, it never merges on its own.
rails.reviewBody: Finished specs park On review. You choose: create a draft PR, integrate locally (no remote needed), or discard. Merge flips them to Done.
rails.packetBody: A plain-language page per delivery: what was asked, what changed, what the AI reports versus what the app verified, the cost — with Accept / Request changes / Discard.
rails.steerBody: Claude runs are interactive: ask questions or redirect while they work, and follow a narrated progress view instead of raw logs.
rails.loopsBody: Loops is a visual builder: chain AI steps, shell commands and a Loop Decider that repeats until a goal is met. Built-in Implement, Batch and Freestyle ship ready to use.
rails.profilesBody: Decide which agents run and which model each uses — per project profile, per rail, or once for the whole machine in Settings → Specrails Agents.
rails.isolationBody: Each project has its own database and queue; your repository stays pristine because Specrails keeps its own files under your home folder.

providers.title: Bring your own agent
providers.subtitle: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Kimi as first-class engines
providers.intro: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Kimi Code are interchangeable engines behind one contract. Whatever is installed and signed in on this machine is detected automatically and offered everywhere — nothing to configure per project.
providers.calloutBody: Pick the engine per spec, per rail, per mission or per terminal launch; the app remembers your last choice per project. Estimated costs are marked with ~; Kimi does not report token or cost data.

cost.title: Track every cent
cost.subtitle: Every billable invocation, recorded and visualized
cost.intro: Every AI invocation — across rails, Quick, Explore, AI edits, SMASH and file summaries — records its lifecycle and provider. Usage and cost fields remain unavailable when a provider, such as Kimi, does not report them.
cost.analyticsBody: A burn-rate hero, daily timeline, top tickets, model breakdown and a cost-vs-turns scatter. Filter by period (7d / 30d / 90d / All) and by surface.
cost.perTicketBody: Each spec's detail shows what it cost and how many turns it took, deep-linking into Analytics filtered to that ticket.
cost.honestBody: Claude cost is provider-billed; Codex and Gemini may be estimated and marked with <mono>~</mono>. Kimi reports neither tokens nor native USD cost, so those fields show as unavailable rather than zero.
cost.budgetsBody: Set a daily budget and a per-job cost alert; the app auto-pauses the queue when you cross the line. Export anything to CSV or JSON.

workspace.title: Make it your workspace
workspace.subtitle: Everything you need without leaving the window
workspace.terminalBody: A real VS-Code-style terminal at the bottom (<mod>{{mod}}</mod> <j>J</j>) — WebGL rendering, search, inline images, drag-drop paths and shell integration. Up to 10 sessions per project.
workspace.codeBody: A read-only file tree and Monaco viewer with plain-language AI summaries and a construction story per file: which spec touched it, when, and why.
workspace.browserBody: Open links, PRs and your dev server inside the app — a native browser pane in the desktop build, with popups that keep OAuth logins working.
workspace.integrationsBody: A per-project marketplace of MCP integrations (Serena semantic navigation is bundled), plus the Specrails MCP server that exposes the app to your own AI tools.
workspace.themesBody: Six built-in themes — specrails, dracula, aurora-light, obsidian-dark, code-rain and galaxy — applied before the UI paints. Settings → Effects switches visual flourishes like the agent's thinking halo.
workspace.chatsBody: Park an Explore or AI-Edit session into a dock chip and pick it back up later — never lost across refreshes or project switches.
workspace.compareBody: Drag a spec to the screen edge and a picker of your other specs slides in — review two of them together, tablet-style.
workspace.desktopBody: Run Specrails in your browser, or grab the signed desktop app (macOS & Windows) that bundles its own server, Node, git and GitHub CLI.

companion.title: Take Specrails with you
companion.subtitle: Specrails Companion — your pipelines, on your phone
companion.intro: Specrails Companion is a web app at specrails.dev/companion-app — open it on your phone (or add it to your Home Screen) to browse the specs board, launch and stop rails, follow live job logs and glance at analytics. No install, no app store.
companion.localBody: Your phone connects straight to this computer — peer-to-peer and encrypted (WebRTC). No cloud relay, no account, and your code never leaves your devices.
companion.downloadHint: Scan the code with your phone's camera, or open specrails.dev/companion-app in its browser.
companion.pairBody: On your phone open specrails.dev/companion-app, then here go to Settings → Mobile companion → Pair web companion and follow the on-screen steps.

moveFast.title: Move at the speed of thought
moveFast.subtitle: Keyboard-first, everywhere
moveFast.paletteBody: Switch projects, run spec commands, jump to any page and find recent jobs — all with fuzzy search.
moveFast.agentBody: Toggle the agent with {{mod}} Shift A; cycle its level with Shift Tab.
moveFast.shortcutsBody: Press <q>?</q> to see the full cheat-sheet.
moveFast.projectsBody: Toggle the left Arc sidebar with <alt>{{alt}}</alt> <mod>{{mod}}</mod> <bkey>B</bkey>.
moveFast.pagesBody: <mod>{{mod}}</mod> <n>1–9</n> jumps to a page; <alt>{{alt}}</alt> <mod>{{mod}}</mod> <n>1–9</n> switches project.
moveFast.outro: That's the tour. Type what you want to build into the mission composer, or add a project from the left sidebar. You can reopen this walkthrough anytime from Settings.

jira.label: Jira integration
jira.body: Back any project with a Jira board — each spec becomes a Jira issue, kept in sync both ways: status follows the rail, and a comment is posted when a job finishes. Configure it per project when you add it, or anytime in Settings.
